1. Local SEO helps nearby customers find your business in Google Maps, the Local Pack, search results, and increasingly AI-powered search.

## What Is Local SEO? How Small Businesses Get Found in Google and AI Search


A customer nearby is ready to hire someone for a service you offer. They search Google Maps, type “electrician near me,” or ask an AI tool who they should call. Your business could be a great fit, but outdated business info, weak reviews, or unclear website content can make a competitor easier to find and choose.


Local SEO (search engine optimization) helps your business appear when nearby customers search for the products or services you offer. It can improve visibility across Google Maps, the Local Pack, and localized organic results. Many of the same signals that support local SEO can also help AI-powered search tools better understand your business.


Where customers search is changing, too. In 2026,[45% of consumers](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/lcrs-ai-trust/) say they’ve used AI tools to find local businesses, up from 6% a year earlier, according to BrightLocal research. That gives small businesses another reason to make their online presence clear, accurate, and trustworthy.


Improving your local visibility can help you compete for more of the searches that turn into calls, appointments, and booked jobs.


[Source](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/lcrs-ai-trust/)


## **What is Local SEO?**


Local SEO, short for local search engine optimization, helps your business appear when nearby customers search for the services you provide. Depending on the search, your business could appear in Google Maps, the Local Pack, and other local search results.


Traditional SEO can help a website appear for a wide range of searches. Local SEO focuses on reaching your local audience when people search for services in the areas you serve, often when they’re ready to call, visit, or hire a business.


### Understanding Local Search vs. Local SEO


[Local search](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-search/) is how customers look for nearby businesses. Local SEO covers the work you do to improve your chances of appearing in those searches and turning that visibility into calls, appointments, and booked jobs.


## **How Google Ranks Local Businesses: Relevance, Distance & Prominence**


[Google considers three main factors](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?utm_source=chatgpt.com) when deciding which businesses to show for a local search: relevance, distance, and prominence. Understanding these[ranking factors](https://www.thryv.com/blog/google-seo-ranking-factors/) can help you focus your local SEO optimization where it can make the biggest difference.


**Factor** **What It Means for Your Business** **What You Can Do**


**Relevance** How well your business matches what someone needs Clearly describe your services, categories, and locations


**Distance** How close your business is to the searcher or location they searched Keep your address or service area accurate


**Prominence** How established and well-known your business appears online Build reviews and maintain accurate information across relevant websites and directories


### Relevance: Match What Customers are Searching For


If you repair water heaters, clean drains, and take emergency plumbing calls, make those services clear on your Google Business Profile (formerly Google My Business) and website. A broader[SEO strategy for small businesses](https://www.thryv.com/blog/seo-for-small-businesses/) , including keyword research, can help you identify the services and questions customers are searching for, then build relevant pages around local queries that could turn into jobs.


### Distance: Show Google Where You Operate


Google considers how far your business is from the person searching or the location included in their search. Accurate location and service-area information helps Google understand where your business operates and helps customers know whether you serve them.


Keep those business details current across your Google Business Profile, website, and local listings. Location pages can provide more information about the communities you serve and strengthen your relevance for[“near me” searches](https://www.thryv.com/blog/near-me-search-local-seo-opportunities/) . For multi-location businesses, give each location accurate information so customers can quickly find the right one.


### Prominence: Build Trust Through Reviews and Citations


Customer reviews, local citations, links, and relevant brand mentions can all contribute to your broader local presence. Local citations help keep key business information consistent across the web, while local link building can help you earn relevant links from chambers of commerce, industry associations, local media, and other credible organizations in your local community. Google also states that review count and positive ratings can contribute to local ranking.


Think about a homeowner comparing two plumbers after a pipe starts leaking. One has dozens of recent customer reviews and consistent information across local directories, while the other has an old phone number and few recent reviews. Those reviews can serve as a trust signal and help the customer feel more confident about who to call.

## **How AI Search Expands Local SEO in 2026**


A customer looking for a roofer might search “roof repair near me” on Google or ask ChatGPT, Gemini, or Google AI Mode, “Who’s a well-reviewed roofer near me that handles storm damage?” Your business now has more places where it could be discovered before that customer decides who to call.


AI-generated answers are also becoming part of Google Search. In fact, in a March 2025 study,[Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) found that about one in five Google searches in its study produced an AI summary.


Clear service and location information, accurate listings, recent reviews, and useful website content give search and AI systems more consistent context about what your business does and where it operates. Visibility varies across AI tools and searches because each tool ultimately determines which businesses appear in its answers.


Focus on making it clear what you do, where you work, and why customers trust you. That same foundation can support[SEO, AEO, and GEO](https://www.thryv.com/blog/seo-vs-aeo-vs-geo-why-its-all-still-seo/) as[AI search](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-is-ai-search/) gives customers more ways to find local businesses.

## **How to Do Local SEO: Step-By-Step Checklist**


You don’t need to tackle every part of local SEO at once. Start with the places customers are most likely to find you, then work through these six steps as time allows.


### 1. Optimize Your Google Business Profile


Start with the information customers need to decide whether to contact you. Choose the right business category, list your services, confirm your hours and service area, and add your current phone number, website, and photos. A complete profile helps Google understand when your business is relevant. It also puts the information customers need to call, visit, or book directly in front of them.


Check your profile whenever something changes. If an HVAC company starts offering emergency service but its profile doesn’t mention it, someone searching for urgent help may call a competitor instead.


### 2. Get Listed Consistently Across Directories


Check that your business name, address, phone number, website, and hours match across the local directories where customers may find you, including platforms such as Apple Maps. Conflicting details can lead to missed calls or leave customers unsure which listing is correct.


If keeping dozens of local listings currently takes too much time,[listing management software](https://www.thryv.com/features/local-listings/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) can make it easier to keep your business information accurate across multiple sites. Thryv’s business listings management software lets you update key details from one place instead of tracking down individual listings.


### 3. Build and Respond to Reviews


Ask customers for honest feedback shortly after you finish the job, while the experience is still fresh. Recent online reviews can give potential customers more confidence to call or book.


The key is to make the request easy. A[Google review link generator](https://www.thryv.com/free-tools/google-review-link-generator/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) gives customers a direct path to leave feedback.


If review requests tend to get forgotten during busy weeks,[Thryv’s automated reviews](https://www.thryv.com/features/automated-reviews/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) can handle the follow-up. For example, after an HVAC technician completes an air conditioner repair, the customer can automatically receive a review request while the team moves on to the next job.[Thryv’s reputation management software](https://www.thryv.com/features/reputation-management/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) brings review management into one place, while AI Review Response helps draft personalized replies faster.


### 4. Add Location and Area Pages to Your Website


Create useful pages for the main towns, cities, or service areas where you want to attract customers. Important distinction: avoid creating near-identical pages that simply swap one city name for another. Each location or service-area page should provide genuinely useful information specific to the customers and services in that area.


Include the services you provide there, neighborhoods you cover, relevant local details, and a clear way to call, book, or request an estimate. For multi-location businesses, give each location its own useful page, and consider a store finder for customer-facing locations.


For example, a Tampa plumber serving Clearwater could create a Clearwater page that explains its drain cleaning, water heater repair, and emergency plumbing services in that area.


If keeping those pages current is the challenge, a[website builder for small business](https://www.thryv.com/features/professional-website/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) can make it easier to update your service and location information as your business grows. Structured data can also give search engines additional context about your business, locations, and services when implemented correctly, although it does not guarantee higher rankings.


### 5. Target Local Keywords in Your Content


Use keyword research to identify localized keywords that reflect both the services customers need and the places where they’re searching. Start with phrases you hear on customer calls, questions in online reviews and social media, and searches bringing people to your website in Google Search Console. A consistent content marketing approach can then help you answer those questions and build useful pages around the services and locations most important to your business.


Pick a few phrases that closely match the services you want more customers to find, then use them naturally on the relevant service or location page. Use location terms where they help customers understand where a service is available rather than forcing city names repeatedly into the copy.


If a plumber sees people searching for “water heater repair in Tampa,” that phrase could fit on its water heater service page alongside answers about repairs, replacement, and scheduling. Answering real local queries gives your business more opportunities to reach a local audience when nearby customers need that service.


### 6. Track What Turns Searches Into Leads


Track what happens after customers find you. Look at calls, form submissions, direction requests, appointments, and booked jobs alongside search traffic and search rankings. Google Business Profile performance, website analytics, and[Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console/about) can help you see which searches and pages are bringing people to your business. A local rank tracker can also help you monitor how your visibility changes for priority searches, but rankings should always be evaluated alongside calls, leads, appointments, and booked work.


If an emergency plumbing page starts attracting more visitors but calls stay flat, check whether the phone number and next step are easy to find. Traffic growth is useful when it leads to more calls, forms, and booked work, so a gap between visits and leads tells you where to focus next.

## **How Long Does Local SEO Take? Is It Worth It?**


Some updates can improve what customers see fairly quickly, such as correcting an inaccurate listing or updating your Google Business Profile. Changes to local search rankings, Local Pack visibility, and lead volume usually take longer to evaluate because results vary based on your market, competition, location, and starting point.


Early progress might show up as increased Google Business Profile discovery, additional visits to service or location pages, or a growing number of recent reviews. Ultimately, look for that visibility to contribute to calls, estimate requests, appointments, and booked jobs.


[K&L Roofing](https://www.thryv.com/case-study/kl-roofing/) offers one example. Its website appeared on page five of Google in its primary service area before working with Thryv. After Thryv took over its website and SEO, K&L reached page one in under four months. Individual results vary based on your market, competition, and starting point.
